title: Sparse dictionary Mirror codes for a bank of logical linear functions
hypothesis: For 192 D=16 linear functions generated by three active atoms from one paid 32-atom shared dictionary, sparse coordinate codes will reproduce heldout outputs at RMSE <=0.01, use at least 20% fewer total serialized bytes than dense int8 dictionary codes, and reduce shared function decode operations in both development seeds.
physical_object: one shared dictionary of 32 flattened 16x16 function atoms, paid in every method
mirror_coordinate: three atom indices and three scalar coefficients per logical function
logical_multiplicity: 192 callable functions, with 128 train and 64 heldout
controls: dense float coefficients over the same dictionary

task.type: synthetic linear function bank generated from a known shared dictionary
task.atom_generation: random orthonormal vectors in flattened 16x16 matrix space
task.encoder: three-step orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) against paid shared atoms; encode every function from its full matrix

selection_metrics: shared decode and OMP operation proxies

storage.authority: actual serialized uncompressed NPZ function-bank bytes
paid_objects: all per-function dense codes OR all sparse indices and values

compute.query: Matrix application costs D^2 MACs. Dense decode costs N*K*D^2 scalar multiply-add proxy. Sparse decode costs N*S*D^2. OMP encoding charges each of three iterations across K atoms and D^2 features; report encoding separately from serving query path.

gates.PROMISING: Both seeds achieve heldout RMSE <=0.01; sparse int8 payload <=0.80x dense int8 payload; sparse decode ops are lower; actual serialization and replay are verified. Report no Mirror-specific claim if OMP control aliases sparse codes.
gates.FAIL: Independent upper is valid but sparse encoding misses frozen quality/storage/compute gates or exact native OMP alias defeats Mirror-specific attribution.
gates.NOT ESTABLISHED: Independent upper cannot reproduce targets or serialization/metric replay fails.

boundaries: This is an aligned synthetic function family with a known shared dictionary prior, not natural function learning.
The dictionary bytes are paid in every representation.
No code-space combination count is called capacity; outputs on heldout functions determine utility.
Fresh seeds remain sealed unless frozen feasibility gates pass and native OMP attribution is resolved.
